d.chapter: Economic Geography — Natural Regions: 2. The Tropical Grassland Region
d.notions: Crop farming, cash crop, food crop, livestock rearing, nomadic pastoralism, transhumance, hunting.
d.focus: Human activities of the Tropical Grassland region: farming, livestock rearing, hunting, lumbering and others.
d.competence: Learners are able to describe the work of farmers and herders around them and explain why herders move with their animals.
objectives: Describe crop farming in the Tropical Grassland region.
Describe livestock rearing, including nomadic pastoralism and transhumance.
Describe hunting, fishing and wood cutting in the Tropical Grassland region.
recall: The resources of the savanna are pasture, farmland, wildlife, water and trees.
People exploit them by farming, livestock rearing, tourism, fishing and cutting trees.
d.recallNote: Check the homework: what did learners find out from farmers or herders?
situation: Every year in November, Adamou, a Fulani herder, leaves his village near Garoua with his cattle. He walks for weeks towards the valleys in the south, and comes back only when the rains return.
His classmate Paul thinks that Adamou's family moves because they do not like to stay in one place.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Paul does not understand why Adamou's family moves every year with their cattle.
When does Adamou leave, and when does he come back?
He leaves in November, at the start of the dry season, and comes back when the rains return.
What can be done so that herders do not need to move so far?
Farmers and herders can grow fodder, store hay and dig wells or small dams for the animals.
d.justification: This lesson will help us to understand the main activities of the people of the savanna, such as farming and livestock rearing.

qa.q: Farmers around Garoua grow cotton to sell and sorghum to eat. What do we call these two kinds of crops?
qa.a: Cotton is a cash crop, grown to be sold. Sorghum is a food crop, grown to feed the family.

qa.q: Which company buys the cotton of farmers in North Cameroon?
qa.a: The cotton is bought by SODECOTON, which gives seeds and fertilisers to farmers and gins the cotton in its factories.

qa.q: Why do farmers in the savanna prepare their fields in May and harvest in October or November?
qa.a: Because crops need rain to grow. The rainy season lasts from May to October.

sum.title: I. Crop Farming
sum.intro: Crop farming in the Tropical Grassland region has the following characteristics:
items: A. Food Crops
Farmers grow sorghum, millet, maize, groundnuts and cowpeas to feed their families.
B. Cash Crops
Farmers grow cotton to sell. In North Cameroon, SODECOTON buys the cotton and gives seeds and fertilisers.
C. Irrigated Farming
Rice is grown on irrigated fields, for example near Lagdo and at Yagoua (SEMRY).
D. Farming Calendar
Farming depends on the rainy season: fields are prepared in May and crops are harvested in October and November.

qa.q: Adamou moves with his cattle every year. Why must he move in the dry season?
qa.a: In the dry season, the grass dries up and water becomes scarce. He moves to find green pasture and water for his animals.

qa.q: What do we call the movement of herders with their animals between the dry-season and wet-season pastures?
qa.a: This seasonal movement is called transhumance. When herders move all the time without a fixed home, it is called nomadic pastoralism.

qa.q: The Maasai of Kenya and Tanzania also rear cattle in the savanna. Why are cattle important for them?
qa.a: Cattle give them milk, meat and blood for food. They are also a sign of wealth and are used to pay the bride price.

sum.title: II. Livestock Rearing
sum.intro: Livestock rearing is a major activity of the savanna. It is practised in the following ways:
items: A. Nomadic Pastoralism
Nomadic pastoralism is the rearing of animals by herders who move from place to place with them, such as the Fulani and the Maasai.
B. Transhumance
Transhumance is the seasonal movement of herders and animals between dry-season and wet-season pastures.
C. Sedentary Rearing
Some farmers keep animals near the village and feed them with crop residues. Ranches rear cattle on the Adamawa plateau.

qa.q: Besides farming and rearing, give two other activities of the people of the savanna.
qa.a: People also hunt, fish in rivers and lakes, cut wood for fuel and building, and guide tourists in national parks.

sum.title: III. Other Activities
sum.intro: The other human activities of the savanna are the following:
items: A. Hunting
People hunt antelopes and other animals for meat. Controlled sport hunting takes place in hunting zones of North Cameroon.
B. Lumbering and Wood Cutting
Trees are cut for firewood, charcoal and building poles. Large-scale lumbering is rare because trees are scattered.
C. Fishing and Tourism
People fish in the Lagdo lake and the Benue. Tourists visit the national parks.

evaluation: What is the difference between a cash crop and a food crop? Give one example of each.
A cash crop is grown to be sold, like cotton. A food crop is grown to feed the family, like sorghum.
Transhumance is the seasonal movement of herders and animals between dry-season and wet-season pastures.
Why is large-scale lumbering rare in the savanna?
It is rare because the trees are scattered and there are few big trees.
remediation: A crop grown to be sold is a ______ crop.
The company that buys cotton in North Cameroon is ______.
Rice is grown on ______ fields near Lagdo.
The seasonal movement of herders and animals is called ______.
Herders who move all the time are called ______ pastoralists.
A cattle-rearing people of Kenya and Tanzania is the ______.
d.remediationAnswers: 1. cash 2. SODECOTON 3. irrigated 4. transhumance 5. nomadic 6. Maasai
